name: Lanyue
best_known_for: China's crewed lunar lander, in development: two astronauts go down in it while Mengzhou waits in orbit
credit: Lanyue (揽月, "embracing the Moon") is the lander for China's crewed landing, planned before 2030. Launched separately on a Long March 10, it meets Mengzhou in lunar orbit, takes two astronauts to the surface with the Tansuo rover and Wangyu suits, and lifts them back to orbit; a propulsion stage brakes the stack out of lunar orbit and is jettisoned near the surface, after which the lander finishes the descent on its own engines. A full-scale integrated landing and take-off test was carried out at a test site in Huailai, Hebei, in August 2025. China plans an uncrewed Lanyue landing and a full uncrewed rehearsal before any crew goes; no landing site has been announced.
